commands.description: Freehand fallback after insert_* feature tools. part_id is required and must be the active part's opaque surf id (a vault path or display name is unknown_part; another id is part_mismatch). commands.name: list_faces
commands.description: Every pickable face on the active part, or on part_id when set (an opaque surf id, never a path or display name). One row per face a viewport click selects, all bodies: id (f0, f1, …), name (feature.role[k] from the helper that built the face: cube1.top, boss.side, extrude2.wall[3]; feature is the marked block id, else <helper>@<n>; absent on faces no helper stamped, such as a hull), feature, role, type (planar, cylindrical, curved), center, normal, axis and radius for cylinders, area, and key. frame is "local" on every result: center, normal, axis and key.at are the part's own frame, including when the part is placed, and they match select_faces. Compose with part_get_transform to reach the assembly. The id is the patch index on this mesh and is only valid until the next remesh; a rerun of the same script keeps every id. Pass the key with the id to joint_pick so a stale id cannot silently pick another face. The whole list on a detailed part is 100 KB or more, so filter it in the tab: filter { kind, normalWithin: { n, deg }, minArea, maxArea, bbox: { min, max }, name, feature, role } keeps only faces that match every given field (the top faces: kind "planar", normalWithin { n: [0, 0, 1], deg: 5 }; every face of one feature: feature "boss"; the tops of every feature: role "top"; name / feature / role take a glob with *). bbox keeps a face whose triangle bounds overlap the box, so a large face is included when the box covers any part of it. page { offset, limit } returns one page; omitting page returns the first 100 faces (limit defaults to 100). The result always carries total (rows after the filter), returned, offset, and limit, and nextOffset when another page remains. Walk pages with { offset: nextOffset } until nextOffset is absent.

The result carries total (rows after the filter), returned, offset, and limit, and nextOffset when another page remains (pass it as the next offset). list_faces uses offset 0 and limit 100 when page or limit is omitted. Other lists return every remaining row when limit is omitted.

commands.name: mold_fit
commands.description: Read-only moldability fit for one part mesh, in the part local frame (the same frame as list_faces). Searches bounding-box axes, large planar normals, and an icosphere (about 80 directions, deduped within 5°, d and -d are one axis). The chosen pull has the least occluded undercut area. Scores within max(2% of the part area, 25 mm²) of that best are tied; box axes and large planar normals win the tie over an icosphere sample, and drafted area breaks the rest. Fit is still good (0 undercut regions), fixable (1 to 4), or not_a_fit (5 or more), plus undercutCount, undercutArea, draftedArea, pull, and pullSource. Pass pull [x, y, z] to score that axis instead and keep its sign. The same result includes wall: a local thickness per triangle, nominal (mode, or the median when no thickness dominates the interior band), max, min, mean, median, and thin and thick regions. Thickness below 0.6× nominal is thin and above 1.5× nominal is thick. Wall thickness follows the geometric normal of each triangle. A stamp only flips that side when it points the other way, so one stamp on a curved face does not steer every facet. A triangle whose own normal is within 0.5° of perpendicular to the pull is zero-draft, not an undercut, and an undercut needs another triangle covering that point. A geometric check for later molding slices, not a supplier DFM. parting on the same result classifies each face by complete visibility (core along +pull, cavity along -pull; zero-draft walls take a neighbour) and keeps one outer parting loop. Stamped edges keep their names. sideActions on the same result clusters those undercuts into slides and lifters, each with a suggested pull. That split is a heuristic. count, slideCount, and lifterCount are the numbers a later tooling adder can use. moldDraft on the same result flags side walls below 1° of draft and lists ejector-pin and sleeve candidate positions. Those candidates are a heuristic. It does not edit CAD draft.

part_id.description: Opaque surf id of the part to score. Omit for the active part.

pull.description: Override pull direction [x, y, z] in the part local frame. The vector is normalized and its sign is kept. Omit to search.

commands.name: mold_pull
commands.description: Set the shared pull reference used by core/cavity, side actions, and mold draft. mode auto searches icosphere and planar candidates, minimizing occluded undercut area and then maximizing drafted area. mode plane uses Top (+Z), Front (+Y), or Right (+X). mode face uses normal [x, y, z] in the part local frame and keeps its sign. Changing it recomputes those three from the same pull. Read-only. It does not edit CAD draft.

mode.description: auto searches. plane uses an origin plane. face uses normal.

plane.description: Origin plane when mode is plane. Top is +Z, Front is +Y, Right is +X.

normal.description: Face normal [x, y, z] in the part local frame when mode is face. The sign is kept.

Omit on to toggle. Read-only. A geometric view of the mold-analysis wall field, not a stress plot and not a quote.

on.description: true shows the thickness heatmap. false restores paint and the part colour. Omit to toggle.

commands.name: mold_parting
commands.description: Show or hide the core and cavity colours on the active part, in the part local frame. on true classifies faces from the mold-analysis pull by complete visibility (core along +pull, cavity along -pull). A face within 0.5° of vertical is zero-draft: it keeps a core or cavity owner and is painted its own colour. The outer parting loop is a polyline. Stamped faces keep their edge names on that loop. on false removes the skin so face paint and the part colour show again. Omit on to toggle. Read-only. Not a CAD draft edit and not a quote.

on.description: true shows core and cavity colours and the outer parting line. false restores paint and the part colour. Omit to toggle.

commands.name: mold_side_actions
commands.description: Show or hide side-action groups on the active part, in the part local frame. on true clusters the mold-analysis undercuts into slides and lifters, each with a suggested pull, and paints those triangles. Slide versus lifter is a heuristic. on false removes the skin so face paint and the part colour show again. Omit on to toggle. Read-only. Not mold CAD and not a quote.

on.description: true shows side-action groups. false restores paint and the part colour. Omit to toggle.

commands.name: mold_draft
commands.description: Show or hide mold-draft violations on the active part, in the part local frame. on true flags side walls below 1° of draft relative to the mold-analysis pull and lists ejector-pin and sleeve candidate counts. Those candidates are a heuristic. on false removes the skin so face paint and the part colour show again. Omit on to toggle. Read-only. Not CAD draft mode, not an automatic draft fix, and not a quote.

on.description: true shows mold-draft violations and ejector counts. false restores paint and the part colour. Omit to toggle.

commands.name: mold_dfm
commands.description: Show or hide the budgetary DFM report for the active part, in the part local frame. on true reads the mold-analysis result and lists fit, pull, wall nominal, thin and thick counts, draft violations, side-action counts, and ejector-pin and sleeve counts. The report says Budgetary analysis and is not a binding supplier DFM. It does not paint a skin and it does not include a price. Stamped meshes list a few parting-line names. An imported mesh says face names are not available. Draft, side actions, and ejectors stay labeled heuristic. on false closes the panel. Omit on to toggle. Read-only.

on.description: true shows the budgetary DFM report. false closes it. Omit to toggle.

commands.name: mold_quote
commands.description: Show or hide the budgetary molding quote for the active part. on true measures the mesh and asks the server to rank anonymized vendors. The panel says Budgetary, not binding. It lists aluminum and steel unit cost, the part-plus-tooling range, and the quantity where steel becomes cheaper. quantity and cavityCount recompute that quote. grade picks a resin from the selected vendor. The server sets the price. on false closes the panel. Omit on to toggle. It does not paint a skin and it does not place an order. Read-only.

on.description: true shows the budgetary quote. false closes it. Omit to toggle.

quantity.description: Parts to amortize tooling over. Omit to keep the current quantity.

cavityCount.description: Cavities in the mold, from 1 to 64. Omit to keep the current count. Not a cavity layout.

grade.description: Resin grade. Omit to keep the current grade, or the partner’s cheapest active grade when none is set.

commands.name: mold_request_firm_quote
commands.description: Ask the selected anonymized vendor for a firm quote. Creates a molding lead for the signed-in user and does not reveal the vendor. The name stays hidden until that user has a human-review lead for the same vendor whose review fee the Stripe webhook marked paid. Until then the result says to pay for review to see the partner. anonLabel picks a row from the open budgetary quote; omit it to use the selected vendor. Does not charge a card, does not email the partner, and does not change the part. Ranking stays fit then price.

anonLabel.description: Public label from the open budgetary quote, such as Partner A. Omit to use the selected vendor.

commands.name: mold_request_human_review
commands.description: Record a human-review lead for the selected anonymized vendor. This call does not charge a card and does not reveal the vendor. The name stays hidden until the Stripe webhook marks that lead paid. anonLabel picks a row from the open budgetary quote; omit it to use the selected vendor. Does not email the partner and does not change the part.

anonLabel.description: Public label from the open budgetary quote, such as Partner A. Omit to use the selected vendor.

commands.name: mold_pay_human_review
commands.description: Open Stripe Checkout for the human-review fee on the selected vendor. The fee comes from the server. If the signed-in user has no human-review lead for that vendor yet, this records one and then opens Checkout. This call does not mark the review paid, does not reveal the vendor, and does not take a card number. The return URL is not payment. anonLabel picks a row from the open budgetary quote; omit it to use the selected vendor. Cancelled or failed checkout leaves the name hidden. Does not email the partner and does not change the part.

anonLabel.description: Public label from the open budgetary quote, such as Partner A. Omit to use the selected vendor.

commands.description: Bodies of the active part's last run, in mesh order: [{ index, at, triangleCount }]. index is insert_move / insert_rotate body_index; at is the centroid move() and rotateAbout() name (insert_move / insert_rotate at, edit_feature at). Empty before the first run.

commands.name: list_feature_edges

commands.name: invoke_helper
commands.description: Prefer this or insert_* over freehand set_script. Insert a helper palette item on the active part, the same compose path as the UI. Working copy only; git_save commits. The result usedSelection says whether the viewport selection was used. A face pick is written into the script by name (facesNamed for a hole, edgesOf for a fillet or chamfer around that face) and is found again on the new mesh after every rebuild, so a second use_selection insert lands on the same face; an edge pick (select_edges { names }, pick sessions, a tap) is written as edgesNamed(part, "faceA~faceB"), the pair of stamped faces it lies between, which also survives edits. Every face has a name (helper roles, fillet1.round / chamfer2.bevel, import@1.f<k>, <block>.f<k> for freehand). Edge picks still clear with the rebuild (re-pick before the next insert), and use_selection: true with nothing selected is no_selection (nothing is written). Build in ribbon order: block out every part of the assembly as plain blocks first (within seconds of the prompt, then screenshot for the user), then Build and Shape, then Polish, then pattern and place; finish each stage across the whole assembly before the next. Features first: insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the fallback for one operation no feature can do (its block starts with // FEATURE-GAP: <missing feature or option> | <why the existing feature did not work>); set_script only rewrites a whole part. Hardware is one part per unique fastener type, one instance patterned to every place it goes. Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. If the geometry engine crashes under this part (out of memory, a wasm abort, or a run past its 30 s budget) the result is ok: false with crash { code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason: wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost, workerRestarted: true } and one failures row with the same code; status.runState is failed. The worker was already replaced and other parts kept building, so do not ask for a reload and do not retry the same script: simplify the part, lower segment counts, or split it into smaller parts, then run it again. When the run past the budget was inside one marked feature block, the part is rebuilt without that block instead: the result is ok: false with one failures row { code: feature_timeout, featureId, featureType, featureLabel, elapsedMs, budgetMs, detail }, status.runState is failed, the other features are built and shown, and status.featureMs (and feature_tree ms) say how long each block took; edit, delete, or undo that feature. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

use_selection.description: Pass current viewport face/edge picks as compose context. A named pick (select_faces { names }, or a click on a face a helper built) is resolved by name in the script (facesNamed for a face, edgesOf for the edges around it) and is found again after every rebuild, so it can be used for several inserts. A pick with no name clears with the rebuild, and use_selection: true with nothing selected is refused with no_selection.

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

featureMs.description: Kernel milliseconds per feature block (by feature_tree id) on the last run that reported; what is expensive on this part

cache.description: Feature memoisation on the last run: blocks = marked blocks, hits = blocks restored from the worker cache instead of re-run, misses = blocks that ran, bytes = the cache size. An edit re-runs only the edited block and the ones after it.

featureCached.description: Feature blocks (by feature_tree id) served from the cache on the last run: true per id

lastGood.description: Only while runState is failed: volume, bbox and bodyCount of this part's last successful run (the solid the viewport still shows), so a failing feature does not blank the numbers

jointFailures.description: Assembly joints that do not solve right now (broken reference or conflict): count and ids. list_joints has each joint with its status and reason.

features.description: Feature strip rows, only with return: "summary" (script is omitted with "status" and "summary")

ms.description: Kernel milliseconds of this block on the last run that reported it

cached.description: True when the last run restored this block from the feature cache instead of running it

Numbers are finite and within ±1000000 mm (positions and deltas included); NaN and Infinity are bad_args. Working copy only; git_save commits. The result usedSelection says whether the viewport selection was used. A face pick is written into the script by name (facesNamed for a hole, edgesOf for a fillet or chamfer around that face) and is found again on the new mesh after every rebuild, so a second use_selection insert lands on the same face; an edge pick (select_edges { names }, pick sessions, a tap) is written as edgesNamed(part, "faceA~faceB"), the pair of stamped faces it lies between, which also survives edits. Every face has a name (helper roles, fillet1.round / chamfer2.bevel, import@1.f<k>, <block>.f<k> for freehand). Edge picks still clear with the rebuild (re-pick before the next insert), and use_selection: true with nothing selected is no_selection (nothing is written). Build in ribbon order: block out every part of the assembly as plain blocks first (within seconds of the prompt, then screenshot for the user), then Build and Shape, then Polish, then pattern and place; finish each stage across the whole assembly before the next. Features first: insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the fallback for one operation no feature can do (its block starts with // FEATURE-GAP: <missing feature or option> | <why the existing feature did not work>); set_script only rewrites a whole part. Hardware is one part per unique fastener type, one instance patterned to every place it goes. Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. If the geometry engine crashes under this part (out of memory, a wasm abort, or a run past its 30 s budget) the result is ok: false with crash { code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason: wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost, workerRestarted: true } and one failures row with the same code; status.runState is failed. The worker was already replaced and other parts kept building, so do not ask for a reload and do not retry the same script: simplify the part, lower segment counts, or split it into smaller parts, then run it again. When the run past the budget was inside one marked feature block, the part is rebuilt without that block instead: the result is ok: false with one failures row { code: feature_timeout, featureId, featureType, featureLabel, elapsedMs, budgetMs, detail }, status.runState is failed, the other features are built and shown, and status.featureMs (and feature_tree ms) say how long each block took; edit, delete, or undo that feature. Writes (defaults): part = hollow(part, 2.5, 'z'); Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

cache.description: Feature memoisation on the last run: blocks = marked blocks, hits = blocks restored from the worker cache instead of re-run, misses = blocks that ran, bytes = the cache size. An edit re-runs only the edited block and the ones after it.

featureCached.description: Feature blocks (by feature_tree id) served from the cache on the last run: true per id

lastGood.description: Only while runState is failed: volume, bbox and bodyCount of this part's last successful run (the solid the viewport still shows), so a failing feature does not blank the numbers

jointFailures.description: Assembly joints that do not solve right now (broken reference or conflict): count and ids. list_joints has each joint with its status and reason.

features.description: Feature strip rows, only with return: "summary" (script is omitted with "status" and "summary")

commands.name: sketch_edit
commands.description: One call edits a saved contour: it reopens the contour in the sketch (as open_feature on its contour:<id> chip does), applies ops in order, saves and closes the sketch (the rail checkmark: the @contour statement is rewritten by id and every extrude, revolve, loft or sweep that names it rebuilds, one undo step), and returns the entities the contour now has (points, lines, arcs, dimensions, constraints with their ids). ops: profile (the edit_feature contour params: points [[u, v], …], width / height / centered, radius / segments, polygon_preset, tool), add (the sketch_add fields), constrain (the sketch_constrain fields: kind, picks or a / b / line / point), dimension (the sketch_dimension fields: kind, value, picks or edge / line / arc / a / b, name), delete { id } and undo; params is shorthand for one leading profile op. Dimensions and constraints are saved in the contour (solveContour({ points, lines, arcs, dimensions, constraints })), so the sketch stays parametric across runs and reopens with them. An op that cannot be applied is an error naming the op index and what to send; the sketch is closed without saving, so no sketch is ever left open. unknown_contour when the id is not a saved contour chip, not_a_contour when it is another feature. If the geometry engine crashes under this part (out of memory, a wasm abort, or a run past its 30 s budget) the result is ok: false with crash { code: geometry_worker_crashed, reason: wasm_abort | out_of_memory | timeout | worker_lost, workerRestarted: true } and one failures row with the same code; status.runState is failed. The worker was already replaced and other parts kept building, so do not ask for a reload and do not retry the same script: simplify the part, lower segment counts, or split it into smaller parts, then run it again. When the run past the budget was inside one marked feature block, the part is rebuilt without that block instead: the result is ok: false with one failures row { code: feature_timeout, featureId, featureType, featureLabel, elapsedMs, budgetMs, detail }, status.runState is failed, the other features are built and shown, and status.featureMs (and feature_tree ms) say how long each block took; edit, delete, or undo that feature. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

op.description: profile: patch the profile (points, width/height/centered, radius/segments, polygon_preset, tool). add: the sketch_add fields (tool, width, height, radius, segments, points, polygon_preset, params). constrain: the sketch_constrain fields (kind, picks or a/b/line/point, side). dimension: the sketch_dimension fields (kind, value, picks or edge/line/arc/a/b, name). delete: id from list_sketch_entities. undo: one sketch step back.

commands.name: create_assembly
commands.description: Seed a blank assembly with one empty part (no demo script, no seed cube: the first insert_* creates the body). Single-flight per tab: overlapping calls return the same assemblyId. Optional name is a non-unique label. No git write. Returns { assemblyId, assemblyName, activeId, partCount }. Build in ribbon order: block out every part of the assembly as plain blocks first (within seconds of the prompt, then screenshot for the user), then Build and Shape, then Polish, then pattern and place; finish each stage across the whole assembly before the next. Features first: insert_code_snippet { gap, why, script } is the fallback for one operation no feature can do (its block starts with // FEATURE-GAP: <missing feature or option> | <why the existing feature did not work>); set_script only rewrites a whole part. Hardware is one part per unique fastener type, one instance patterned to every place it goes. Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

commands.name: joint_create
commands.description: Fix one base part with a fixed joint, then place every part that touches or attaches to another with joint_create (one call creates the joint and solves placement). Use part_set_transform only for parts that touch nothing. Block-out positions are rough; joints set final positions. Prefer this over hand-computed part_set_transform numbers: one call creates a joint and solves the placement. type is coincident, parallel, perpendicular, distance, angle, concentric, symmetric or fixed (planar is coincident); picks are one row per reference from list_faces (face_id with its key from the same row; a cylindrical face is an axis pick; a face_id is never an ambiguous axis; { part_id } alone is a whole-part pick), one pick for fixed and two for every other type; name, value_mm, sense and opposed as on joint_set_params. Runs the same open → pick → set params → commit path as the Joints card (the advanced path) and records one assembly undo step. The result carries jointId, type, name, valueMm, pickCount and placements: the position and rotation of every picked part after the solve. A pick that does not resolve is unknown_part / unknown_face, and a joint the solver refuses is joint_unsolvable with details.reason and, when more than one axis matches, details.candidates (id, origin, direction, radius); in both cases nothing is written and no card is left open. usedSelection is always false: the picks are explicit. The solve re-runs every joint, so when this joint leaves another one failing the result adds warning { code: "joint_broken", joints, hint } and still succeeds. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

commands.name: git_save
commands.description: The only vault content write, same planSave path as the Save button. message required. Working-copy tools do not commit. consent_pending: Allow dialog is up; retry the same call after the user clicks Allow. pending_save: an offline plan is waiting; Save again when online. upgrade_required: legacy vault; call git_upgrade_vault { confirm: true } after the user agrees. conflict or repo-moved: a remote edit overlaps this Save; git_force_overwrite, or git_behind_resolve { action: "reload" | "branch", confirm: true }, or stop. Results omit path fields. Over the wire a save is many GitHub round trips: when it is still running after about 20 s the call answers { status: "running", saveId } and the save keeps going; poll git_save_status { save_id } until it answers the save result (committed, clean, or the same errors). Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.

commands.name: git_save_status
commands.description: The outcome of a git_save that answered { status: "running", saveId }: { status: "running", saveId, elapsedMs } while the save is still on the wire, else exactly what git_save would have returned (committed with sha, clean, or its error such as conflict). Read-only and immediate. unknown_save: no save with that id ran past the budget in this tab (git_save answers its result directly when it finishes in time), or it finished more than 10 minutes ago.

save_id.description: saveId from a git_save that answered status running

commands.name: git_upgrade_vault
commands.description: Upgrade a legacy (v1 folder-layout) vault to v2 in one commit of remote tip bytes, then Save a dirty working copy as a second commit under the same confirmation. Requires confirm: true. Never runs on load. On v2 returns already_upgraded. Success is a summary: status, commit SHAs, assemblyIds, counts, leftoverFiles paths, and warnings — not the full plan, file contents, meshes, partBindings paths, or rekey.scripts. Takes return: "status" | "summary" | "full" (MCP default "status": status.script is omitted; "summary" adds status.features; "full" echoes the script).

return.description: How much of status to return: "status" drops status.script, "summary" drops it and adds status.features (the feature strip), "full" keeps the whole script. Over MCP the default is "status"; in the page it is "full". Read the script with get_script.
